steps: Pre-installation checks
Unpack and inspect every part, and check clearances to all nearby combustibles. Attach the supplied metal label (3300-148) to the fireplace before the insert goes in.

Pack list: the insert (façade, ash lip with blower and top grill in place), 2 catalysts in the firebox, the surround kit box on top, and in the firebox two refractory stone kit boxes (A and B), a wood handle kit (2 handles and 2 screws), the owner's manual packet and, on enamel models, touch-up paint.

  • Report damaged or missing parts to the dealer immediately.
  • Check clearances to walls, floor, ceiling, mantel and chimney decor before connecting anything.
  • With all chimneys, make a positive connection between the flue collar and the chimney.
  • The manual says the insert should not be installed in a factory-built fireplace; see the conflict note under Chimney liner.
Chimney & liner

Have a professional check the masonry chimney and finish any repairs; remove the damper or lock it open. Run a listed 6" stainless steel liner the full length and seal the damper area against room air.

• Masonry chimney wall: brick, modular block, rubble or stone at least 4" (102 mm) thick. Ceramic flue liner at least 5/8" (16 mm) thick in refractory mortar with at least 1" (25 mm) air space, or an equivalent listed class 3 liner system (ULC-S635 or ULC-S640).
  • Seal the damper area with a sealed block off plate or a plug of noncombustible material such as unfaced fiberglass insulation.
  • Secure every joint, including liner to flue collar, with three #10 x 1/2" sheet metal screws in the pre-drilled holes. No aluminum or galvanized steel pipe.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar from the fireplace. Exception: masonry or steel (including the damper plate) from the smoke shelf and damper frame, if needed for the liner and the removal won't weaken the structure or reduce clearance protection below the National Building Code.
  • Prefabricated metal chimney: full height listed liner, room air kept out of the chimney cavity, louvers and cooling air ports unblocked, no blocked circulating chambers, a way to remove the insert for flue cleaning, and the permanent metal warning label riveted to the outside wall.
  • Choose an interior chimney where possible; an exterior chimney runs cooler, drafts less and builds creosote faster.
Floor protection

Protect combustible flooring with noncombustible material (slate, marble tiles or similar) extending past the insert body as drawn on this page. Use R1.5 insulation beneath it, or set the insert bottom at least 7" above it with R0.

How far the protection must extend, and the minimum fireplace dimensions, are shown only as drawings (Figures 2 and 4) on this page. The masonry fireplace must be built to NFPA211 standards.

Luxury vinyl plank or tile can begin to warp at 110° Fahrenheit. Check the flooring maker's temperature limits; extra shielding may be needed.
Unpack & off the pallet

Empty the firebox (manual packet, two boxes of soapstone, the catalysts, touch-up paint). Remove the ash lip, grill, bypass knob and façade, then the four pallet clips and lag bolts with a 1/2" wrench.

1. Ash lip: back out the setscrews just below both front corners. With the door open wide, lift the front edge slightly (don't touch the door), slide it left (right if the hinges are on the left) and out from under the door. Remove the grill, and the bypass knob from the push-pull rod.
  2. Façade: close the door to within 1 inch with the handle at 12 o'clock. Grip the façade by the sides near ash lip height, pull the bottom out about 2 inches to clear the door and handle, lift slightly and slide it off the bypass rod.
  3. Pallet: four mounting clips on the leveling bolts (two front, under the façade, and two back) hold the insert down. Remove the lag bolts and clips with a 1/2" wrench.
Handle enamel parts with care.
Flue collar onto the liner

Remove the baffle halves and the access plate (7/16" socket), then unbolt the flue collar through the door opening. Fasten it to the liner with three screws, vertical or at 30 degrees, near its final height with the lock bolts parallel to the back wall.

1. Lift the right side of the baffle support off the stone retainer, slide it right and detach it from the left. Slide the baffle halves out to the front one at a time; they break if bumped or crushed.
  2. Remove the access plate with a 7/16" socket wrench.
  3. Remove the flue collar (the bolts are visible through the bypass door opening). Hand tighten the bolts so the long section of the locks points to center.
  4. Attach the collar to the liner with three screws, adjust its position and seal the remaining chimney opening.
Level before you set it: check the fireplace floor for uneven bricks or stones where the levelers sit. Install level or tilted slightly back so the door won't swing open on its own. The rear leveling bolts can only be adjusted before the unit is installed. On a very uneven hearth, slide it in on a piece of sheet metal.
Bracket, façade & options

Attach the surround mounting bracket (kit 94-5991110 instructions). If the bracket would block the façade later, check the catalyst probe, do any door or power cord reversal, and refit the façade and grill now.

To mount the façade, pull the bypass rod out (knob removed) and reverse the removal. Let the clips on the top rear corners drop into the cast pockets, or the crossbar won't fit the groove under the door. Enameled grills have screws in the bottom corners that hold the grill slightly above the façade; they shouldn't need adjusting.

Optional, before final installation

  • Reverse the door to open from the right (hinges on the left): mark the hinge screw heads, move the hinges with a 5/32 (4mm) hex wrench, swap the latch catch and door stop, plug the old holes with the saved screws, then adjust hinges, stop and latch until the gasket seals. Set the door stop so the door can't touch the surround (pp. 20–21).
  • Move the blower cord from the right side to the left: remove the façade and the ash lip assembly and move the cord's wire loops to the matching spots on the left, with one loop on the screw nearest the corner so the cord can't rub the blower housing. Don't disconnect any power cord wiring; there is enough length. Check that the air control moves freely afterwards (p. 23).
Set the insert & lock the collar

Move the insert into position, level, centered and parallel to the fireplace; confirm the collar through the bypass door opening. Pull the collar into place with the flue collar locks, capture each short arm between the cast stops, then tighten.
While tightening, keep the lock bolts parallel to the stove and make sure the rib on the bottom of the collar is seated in the gasket groove on top of the insert.
Baffle, ash lip & stone

Reinstall the baffle, then the ash lip (its rear seals against the gasket under the door to keep ash out of the blower area). Lay in the soapstone in the listed order: floor stones are in box B, side and back stones in box A.

Sort the stones by size on a piece of cardboard first. Install side stones far to the front and slide them back under the stone retainer.

  1. Stone D (2 stones), center rear wall (1-0000-103)
  2. Stone E (2 stones), side wall (1-0400-904)
  3. Stone F (2 stones), side wall (1-0400-905)
  4. Stone A (2 stones), front floor outer (1-0000-101)
  5. Stone A (2 stones), rear floor outer (1-0000-101); don't push them to the back wall yet
  6. Stone D (2 stones), outer rear wall (1-0000-103), one at a time; hold each up and push the floor stone under it
  7. Stone C (1 stone), front square floor (1-0400-902)
  8. Stone A (1 stone), front sideways floor (1-0000-101)
  9. Stone B (1 stone), rear floor center (1-0000-001)
Note: The manual gives two rear wall orders: p. 18 installs the center rear wall stones first and the outer rear wall stones at step 6, while p. 31 (replacing stones) lists the outer rear stones first and the inner rear stones at step 6.

The ash lip may be tight and need some downward force at the front. Be careful with enamel parts.
Catalysts & surround

Once the chimney liner is in, set the two catalysts through the access hole into their pockets on either side of the opening (no gasket needed) and refit the access hole cover. Assemble the surround per its own instructions.
The surround panels, assembly hardware and mounting bracket come in the large cardboard box shipped with the insert. The first fires must follow the break-in procedure (p. 27).

panels.title: Stove smokes or back-puffs
items: Opening technique → open the air fully a minute before opening the door, and open the bypass first
Cold chimney or reverse draft → preheat the chimney; briefly open a window
Blocked, oversized, undersized or too-short chimney → clear it, reline, add a draft inducer or lengthen it
Air leaks into the chimney, or another appliance on the flue → seal openings; disconnect other appliances
Bypass not closed with catalysts active, or catalysts not working → close it; inspect and brush the catalysts
Extra low burn rate or chimney down-draft → burn hotter; install a chimney cap

panels.title: Uncontrolled or short burn
items: Unsealed or open door, or air leaking at the glass gasket → close it tightly; replace the gaskets
Excessive draft → operate at low burn; correct draft over 0.1 wc with a stovepipe damper
Extra long or oversized chimney → shorten or reline it; stovepipe damper(s)
High winds or hilltop location → install a chimney cap

panels.title: Insufficient heat
items: Poor quality, low Btu or green wood → air-dried wood, preferably dried at least one year
Low burn rate → operate at a higher burn rate
Cold exterior chimney → reline or insulate it
Leaky stovepipe or chimney, or heat loss from the house → check the installation; insulate and seal
Excessive ash build-up → empty ashes more often

panels.title: Catalyst problems
items: Fly ash build-up → light-off not maintained, char-heavy materials or bypass closed too soon; brush the cold combustor
Plugging or masking → wet or pitchy wood, or bypass closed before light-off; burn dry wood and run hot for one hour
Warping or bowing → catalysts too hot for long periods; reduce the air setting

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Use these steps for everyday fires. For a new insert, or the first fire of each season, follow the break-in steps instead.

  1. Pull the bypass handle out to open the bypass.
  2. Open the door. Put five or six double sheets of tightly twisted newspaper in the center of the firebox. Crisscross about ten pieces of kindling on top, about 1/2" thick and 10" to 18" long. You can add two or three small logs.
  3. Pull the primary air control fully out.
  4. Light the paper. Leave the door slightly ajar until the kindling is burning and the draft starts to pull.
  5. Close the door. Once the kindling burns well, add small logs, then larger pieces. Keep logs away from the glass.
  6. When the thermometer reaches Catalyst Active, push the bypass handle in to close it.
  7. Set the burn with the air control: out for a hotter fire, in for a slower one.

Reloading

Open the bypass before you open the door. Open the door just a crack, pause, then open it fully so the smoke clears. Load onto a bed of hot, red coals, and load gently: the ceramic baffle breaks if wood hits it. Close the bypass again once the thermometer is back in the active range.

breakin.title: Break-in fires
breakin.html:
Break your insert in slowly. The cast iron needs seasoning and the soapstone lining needs to dry out gently; over-firing a new insert can crack the castings. Build your first fire, and the first fire of every season, like this:

  1. Pull the bypass handle out to open the bypass.
  2. Open the door. Put five or six double sheets of tightly twisted newspaper in the center, with about ten pieces of kindling (1/2" thick, 10" to 18" long) crisscrossed on top.
  3. Pull the primary air control fully out.
  4. Light the paper. Leave the door slightly ajar for a moment, until the kindling catches and the draft pulls.
  5. Close the door. Keep a steady, low-heat fire: the insert should get warm, but not hot to the touch. Add a few small chunks of wood at most.
  6. Once it's warm, push the air control fully in and let the fire die out completely.
  7. Let the insert return to room temperature.
Smoke and smells are normal at first. Paints and oils burn off, usually for 10 to 20 minutes. Open a few windows. If an odor persists, call your dealer.

Do this again if the insert hasn't been used in quite some time. Creosote can build up fast during break-in, so check the stovepipe and chimney (and clean them if needed) once it's done.

bypass.title: Bypass & catalyst thermometer
bypass.html:
Your insert has two catalysts that burn up smoke the fire leaves behind. The bypass sends smoke around them until they're hot enough to work, and the catalyst thermometer shows you where you are.

Inactivebypass open (handle pulled out) until the stove heats up
Catalyst Activebypass closed (handle pushed in)
Too Hotkeep the door closed, close the air control fully and let it cool back to Active
  • Open the bypass when you start a fire, and every time before you open the door to load.
  • From a cold start, keep a medium to high fire going for about 20 minutes. If the fire dies down too soon, it may go out or the catalysts may stop working.
  • The catalysts become active around 500 °F. The Clydesdale typically runs in the 800 °F to 1300 °F range.

When the catalysts are working, you should see little to no smoke from your chimney.

Never run it without the catalysts. It's against federal regulations to operate this heater with the catalytic element removed or deactivated.

burn.title: Air control & burn rates
burn.html:
The primary air control handle is at the front center of the ash lip, under the ash lip cover. Pull it out for more air and a faster, hotter fire. Push it in for a slower burn. It never shuts the air off completely.

Highair fully or almost fully open, firebox fully loaded; once or twice a day
Medium to medium lowmid-range; the most efficient overall burn
Lowair closed; the longest burn, but it builds creosote, so only now and then

Overnight

With the stove and chimney hot, open the air fully and fill the firebox; bigger pieces burn longer. Let it burn hard for 20 to 30 minutes, then push the air control close to its lowest setting. In the morning, rake the hot coals to the surface, add a handful of kindling and a few small logs, close the door and open the air fully. It should catch within 5 to 10 minutes.

Don't over-fire. The top front of the insert, under the grill, shouldn't routinely go above 600° Fahrenheit. Short burn times, a roaring sound or a discolored finish are warning signs. If you suspect the insert is over-firing, contact your dealer immediately. Over-firing damage isn't covered by the warranty.

The blower runs only when the insert is hot. Its speed control is the notched wheel at the bottom center of the ash lip.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural cordwood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives you the best efficiency and the lowest emissions.

  • Burn only clean, dry, seasoned firewood. Wet wood greatly reduces your efficiency and can greatly affect the insert's emissions.
  • Seasoned wood is typically at or below 20% moisture. A hand-held moisture meter will tell you.
  • To season green wood, split it, stack it and let it air dry for a year. Keep the stack off the ground on skids or blocking and cover only the top.
  • Hardwoods burn longer and leave longer-lasting coals; softwoods burn hotter and faster. The chart on this page ranks common species by heat content.
  • Logs up to 22" long fit.
  • Don't put ice-covered wood into a hot stove, and don't store firewood within the insert's clearances.
Never burn garbage or trash, lawn clippings, cardboard, paper products (including glossy paper), plywood or particleboard, painted, treated (including pressure-treated) or kiln dried wood, unseasoned (wet or green) wood, coal, charcoal, pellets, artificial or wax logs, railroad ties, asphalt products, construction or demolition debris, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners, solvents, manure or animal remains, flammable fluids, anything containing asbestos, plastic or rubber (including tires), or driftwood (including salt water driftwood) and other previously saltwater saturated materials. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes or make the insert ineffective and cause smoke. Never use chemicals or flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or engine oil to start a fire. These fuels cause dangerous burning conditions in the stove. Keep all such materials away from the insert. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Empty the ashes at the end of every week, or sooner if the firebox is full. You can leave a thin layer in the firebox.

  1. Let the fire die down or go out completely.
  2. Push large live coals to the side and remove only the finer ash with a fireplace shovel. Don't let ash build up at the door opening: it can spill out or pack into the gasket channel.
  3. Put the ashes straight into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Nothing else goes in, and don't pour water in.
  4. Close the lid. Set the container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that burns, liquid fuels and vehicles. Never on a combustible surface or vinyl flooring.
  5. Keep the ashes in the closed container until all the coals are thoroughly cool.
Coals in ash can stay hot for several days. Never put ashes in wooden or plastic containers, paper or plastic bags, or a trash can with other trash.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the fire is out and the glass is cool. Use a low alkaline content commercial stove glass cleaner (your dealer has them) and follow its instructions.

For heavier deposits

Take the door off, saving the hinge pins and spacers. Lay it face down on a bench with the handle hanging over the edge, apply the cleaner and let it sit a few minutes, then wipe it off with a soft cloth.

No razor blades, steel wool or other abrasives. Scratching or etching weakens the glass.
  • Never use the insert with broken glass. Replace it right away with Hearthstone's ceramic glass (glass kit 94-58910, from your dealer).
  • Don't strike or slam the door.
  • Keep logs away from the glass so the air-wash system works. A daily hot fire also helps keep it clean.

care.title: Chimney care & upkeep
care.html:
Slow, cool fires leave creosote, a tar that collects in the chimney and can ignite into a very hot chimney fire.

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season, and at least monthly if creosote is building up. Remove it before it's more than 1/4" (6 mm) thick; a certified chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Have the whole system professionally inspected and cleaned before each heating season.
Note: The manual gives different hot-burn times: p. 33 says to burn with the air fully open for 35 - 45 minutes daily and for 15 to 20 minutes after reloading; p. 28 gives about 20 minutes for the daily high burn and p. 29 about 10 minutes at a medium to high rate after rekindling.

Regular checks

  • Every other month: the dollar bill test. On a cool stove, shut the door on a dollar bill. If it pulls out with no resistance, adjust the latch or replace the gasket. Also vacuum any fly ash off the face of the catalysts with a soft brush attachment.
  • Each season's end: clean out the firebox, replace a worn or hard door gasket and any badly cracked soapstone, and clean the blower under the ash lip cover.

safety.title: Safety & chimney fires
safety.html:
• Keep children and pets away while it's burning. A hot stove can seriously injure them.
  • Keep furniture, drapes, clothing and other combustibles at least 36" (0.92 m) from the stove.
  • Never use gasoline, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or other flammable fluids to start or liven up a fire.
  • Install smoke and CO detectors throughout the heated space, including bedrooms and hallways, and test them. Keep an "A B C" rated fire extinguisher handy.
Note: The manual says to operate only with the door fully closed on p. 24 and p. 29, but p. 29 also says the door must be fully closed or opened completely (e.g. when using viewing screen).

If you have a chimney fire

  1. If it's too threatening, leave and call the fire department immediately.
  2. If not, close the primary air control, the stovepipe damper (if there is one) and the bypass. Keep the front door closed.
  3. Let the fire die out completely. Inspect the stove, stovepipe and chimney thoroughly, and fix any damage, before you use it again.
Never throw water on the stove, stovepipe or chimney. The extreme heat turns it to steam instantly and can cause serious harm.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hearthstone's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser only, on an insert installed by an authorized Hearthstone dealer or their representative. It starts on the original invoice date and can't be transferred. "Limited Lifetime" means 10 years.

Stone, cast iron not listed elsewhereLimited Lifetime
Door handles and latches, steel components and firebox5 years
Electrical and gas components2 years
Enamel finish, accessories, glass, all other components1 year
Note: The table on p. 40 lists glass at 1 year, but p. 41 excludes repair or replacement of wear parts, glass included.

Applied Ceramics covers the catalysts: no-charge replacement within two years, then a prorated price from $130.00 in year 3 to $160.00 in year 6. Keep your bill of sale.

Note: p. 39 says a catalyst that stops working within two (2) years is replaced at no charge, but the same page also refers to one replacement catalyst for each defective catalyst returned during the three year period.

Over-firing, wrong fuels and installation or use not per the manual void coverage. To claim, contact your Hearthstone dealer.

specOutput.title: Heat output
specOutput.html:
Maximum heat output60,000 BTU per hour of cordwood
EPA test output range14,829 to 32,588 Btu
Size of heated areaUp to 2,000 square feet

The 60,000 BTU per hour maximum is based on independent laboratory test results (p. 7). The 14,829 to 32,588 Btu range is what the insert delivered under the specific EPA test conditions (p. 2). An oversized insert is often forced to burn at a lower, dirtier rate, so size it to the space.

specEmissions.html:

Weighted average efficiency79% (HHV)

Certified to the EPA 2015 particulate emissions standard and approved for sale after May 15, 2020; tested to EPA Method 28, 28A and 5H. Efficiency was measured with EPA Method 28R and CSA B415-10 across all 4 burn rate categories. The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered (federal regulations).

specFirebox.title: Firebox
specFirebox.html:

The 48-pound figure assumes 20 lbs. of seasoned hardwood per cubic foot; real loads vary from 15 to 36 lbs. per cubic foot. The firebox is lined with soapstone and the fire burns directly on the floor stones, with no grate. The two catalysts are reached by removing the baffle and the catalyst access plate.

Install a continuous liner from the insert to the top of the chimney, with a positive connection at the flue collar. Never share a flue with another appliance or connect to air distribution ductwork. The chimney must be at least 3 feet (0.9 m) above the highest part of the roof opening it passes through and at least 2 feet (0.6 m) above any part of the roof within 10 feet (3 m). Draft in excess of 0.1 wc should be corrected with a stovepipe damper.

Note: p. 4 and p. 8 say the insert should not be installed in a factory-built fireplace, but p. 9 lists the conditions for installing it in a fireplace with a prefabricated metal chimney.
Note: p. 10 requires a listed 6" stainless steel liner the full length of a masonry chimney, but the same page says an 8" (203 mm) existing flue can be used with a reducer.

conflicts.issue: Factory-built fireplaces: pp. 4 and 8 say the insert should not be installed in a factory-built fireplace, but p. 9 lists the conditions for installing it in a fireplace with a prefabricated metal chimney (full-height listed liner, louvers/cooling air ports unblocked, riveted warning label).

Liner size: p. 10 requires a listed 6" stainless steel liner the full length of a masonry chimney (p. 9: continuous liner, minimum 6"), but p. 10 also says an 8" (203 mm) existing flue can be used with a reducer.
Width printed as 31.38" with 80.31 cm alongside on p. 7; the two figures don't agree (height, depth, log length and door size conversions do).
Daily creosote burn: about 20 minutes or so of high burn (p. 28) vs primary air fully open for 35 - 45 minutes daily (p. 33).
After reloading: medium to high firing rate for about 10 minutes when rekindling a cool fire (p. 29) vs primary air fully open for 15 to 20 minutes after reloading (p. 33).

Open-door operation: only operate with the door fully closed (p. 24) and the front door must remain closed when in operation (p. 29), but p. 29 also says the door must be fully closed or opened completely (e.g. when using viewing screen). No screen is listed among parts or accessories (p. 37).
Refractory stone order: p. 18 installs the center rear wall stones (D) first and the outer rear wall stones at step 6; p. 31 lists the outer rear stones first and the inner rear stones at step 6.
Glass coverage: the component table lists glass at 1 Year (p. 40), but exclusion 3 lists glass (with paint, gaskets, baffles, refractory, ash grates) as a wear part not covered (p. 41).

Catalyst warranty period: no-charge replacement if the combustor ceases to function within two (2) years, then 'one replacement catalyst for each defective catalyst returned during the three year period' on the same page; the section is also headed 'Limited Lifetime' while the terms run to year 6 prorated.

review.notes: Clearances to the mantel, trim and walls, the floor-protection extension and the minimum fireplace dimensions exist only as dimension drawings (Figures 2 and 4 on p. 12; shielded/unprotected mantel drawings on p. 13), so no values were transcribed; the catalog clearances_note and the 'minimum fireplace opening 32-1/2 x 23-1/4 x 13 in.' feature could not be checked against the text. The catalyst replacement measurement range (p. 31, 'range shown below') is also figure-only and was not transcribed. The warranty grid (p. 40) is a check-mark table: only rows marked in all three fuel columns were transcribed; partially marked rows (clean burning air supply system, burner and logs, burn pot and baffles, refractory/vermiculite panels/baffles, ash grate) were left out because the column alignment is lost in the text. p. 2 prints the emission rate as '1.16 gr/hr.' (kept as printed; the catalog's 1.16 g/hr matches the number). Heat output: 60,000 BTU per hour maximum (p. 7, independent lab, cordwood) and the EPA test range 14,829 to 32,588 Btu (p. 2) are different test bases as the manual states; both shown, not flagged as a conflict. Detector placement differs slightly (p. 2: also in the area where the appliance is located; p. 5: preferably in an area away from the stove); the guide gives only the general 'throughout the heated space' advice. The glass replacement steps (p. 32) skip fitting the new glass; not reproduced (the glass kit has its own instructions). The blower cord re-routing (p. 23) has you disconnect the temperature snap disk wires but never says to reconnect them; the guide only summarizes and points to p. 23. The table of contents lists 'Outside air supply', but there is no such section; p. 34 only mentions an optional outside air adaptor (no part number), so there is no outside-air card. The manual gives no blower electrical rating, so there is no electrical card. The troubleshooting chart says 'empty the ash pan' though the insert has no ash pan; the guide says 'empty ashes'. The emergency procedure says 'perform the next three steps' but lists four. Cross-references on pp. 5-6 to page 3 (creosote) and page 9 (36" clearance) point to the wrong pages. The safety label (p. 38), Figure A (p. 11) and p. 14 are images only. No French-only or scrambled text.
